description: Like a JavaScript let: the binding may change. Plain let acts like const and also freezes the value.
Subtraction that returns None on overflow, where JavaScript would return a negative Number.
A final expression without a semicolon is returned, like an arrow function's expression body.
An exhaustive switch: no fall-through, and every possible value must be covered.
A method receiver that may change fields; in a JavaScript class every method can change this.
A discriminated union whose variant is the tag, checked by the compiler.
Replaces null and undefined: Some(value) or None, handled before the value is used.
A lazy map or filter that runs only when a consumer such as sum pulls items.
Update-or-insert with one lookup, replacing map.set(k, (map.get(k) ?? 0) + 1).
Iterates Unicode scalar values, while JavaScript's length counts UTF-16 code units.
Assigning a String hands it to a new owner, where JavaScript would share one reference.
Exclusive borrowed access, the only way a function may change its argument.
A nominal interface: a type satisfies it only through an explicit impl block.
Replaces throw: failure is a return value that the caller must handle.
Records the exact resolved dependency versions, like package-lock.json.
A lazy Promise: nothing runs until an executor polls it.
